QUAD 34 · PREAMPLIFIER

Restoring your Quad 34

The Quad 34 is a preamplifier from the 1980s. It chooses your source and sets volume and tone, and it has a phono stage for turntables.

This guide is new. Nobody has checked its parts list against a real Quad 34 yet, so treat it as a starting point.

Before anything else: stay safe

This preamplifier plugs into the mains. Parts inside can still give you a dangerous shock after it is unplugged.

If you are new to electronics, don't open it. You can do everything on this page from the outside. A qualified technician does the work inside.

Four steps

1

Write down a few details

You can find all of these from the outside.

  • The serial number. It decides which parts list applies.
  • The finish (brown or grey) and whether the inputs on the back are round DIN sockets or RCA (phono) sockets.
  • Your turntable cartridge, if you use one, and whether it is moving magnet or moving coil.
  • The fuse rating printed on the back panel.
  • Anything already done to it, such as an earlier recap.
2

Talk it through with an AI assistant

An AI assistant with the Quad Agent guide checks your details against Quad's own documents and tells you what applies to your Quad 34. It asks questions first and never guesses part values.

Copy this into your AI assistant:

Read quad-upgrade/SKILL.md and follow it to help me restore my Quad 34. Start by helping me identify it from the outside.

It needs the guide files first. Download the guide and add it to your assistant, or give it the quad-upgrade folder.

3

Choose what you want done

The recap

The 34's capacitors and chips age. A recap replaces the capacitors and, with DADA's kit, fits better modern chips. It is the most common job and the best place to start.

Optional extras

These change how the Quad 34 behaves. You don't need any of them.

  • Phono stage changes. There are changes for moving magnet and moving coil cartridges, and a way to turn the phono input into an extra line input if you use a separate phono stage.
  • Output level and balance control fixes. For when the 34 is too loud for its power amp, or the balance control has become noisy.
4

Take it to a technician

Send them the link to this page. Everything they need is in the section below: the parts list, Quad's service documents and the upgrade guides.

Ask them to check the parts against your actual Quad 34 before ordering. Quad changed things during production, and earlier owners may have too.

Good to know

  • Units at exactly serial 8000 sit between two parts lists. A technician needs to look at the board before parts are ordered.
  • On some capacitors the markings on the board are known to be wrong. The guide tells the technician which way round they go.
  • Always fit the fuse rating shown on your unit's back panel.

For your technician

Parts list

Provisional. Every part comes from a named document but has not yet been checked against a real board. Confirm against the actual board before ordering. The recap comes first; optional changes are listed separately.
